question: How many litre of water can a hemispherical bowl of diameter 21 m hold? (1 m³ = 1000 litre)
solution:
**Given:**

The diameter of the hemispherical bowl is 21 m 

(1 m3 = 1000 litre)

**Formula used:**

Volume of a hemispherical bowl is = 2 / 3 πr²h

( r = radius, h = height)

**Concept used:**

Radius = Diameter / 2

**Calculation:**

Volume of a hemispherical bowl is = 2 / 3 πr³

⇒ 2 / 3 π (21 / 2)³

⇒ (2 / 3) × (22 / 7) × (21 / 2) × (21 / 2) × (21 / 2) 

⇒ 22 × (21 / 2) × (21 / 2) 

⇒ 4851 / 2 

= 2425.5 m³

Now, 1m³ = 1000 litre

So, 2425.5 m³ = 2425500 litre

**∴ 2425500 litre of water can be hold**
